topic: Debt Snowball vs Debt Avalanche: Which Actually Works

sections.voiceover: The snowball versus avalanche debate is a $215 question. Not choosing at all costs you $13,600.
sections.visual_cue: Black screen. "$215" slams in center in large Inter, then "$13,600" replaces it. Dark background #0A1020, accent #22C55E.
sections.sfx_cue: Sharp tick on each number. Silence after "$13,600."
sections.pacing_notes: Numbers are the hook. Deliver flat, then stop.

sections.voiceover:
Avalanche pays the highest interest first. It wins the math. On a realistic $10,636 in debt, it finished in 27 months with $2,838 in interest. Snowball pays the smallest balance first. It took 28 months and $3,053. A gap of just $215.

But the calculators miss the point. A Kellogg study of 6,000 debt settlement clients found the people who actually finished were the ones who closed accounts early. The snowball closes its first account in month four. The avalanche closes nothing until month ten. Small wins keep people going.
sections.visual_cue: Kinetic text blocks on #1E293B. Each fact its own screen, 3-6 words per line. Key numbers in #22C55E. Brief pause before "But the calculators miss the point."
sections.sfx_cue: Typing sounds as text appears. Bass hit on "month ten."

text_overlay.text: Snowball closes in month 4. Avalanche month 10.

sections.pacing_notes: Fast, punchy. Each sentence is a hammer. Pause 0.5s before the Kellogg turn.
research_sources: Gal & McShane, 'Can Small Victories Help Win the War?', Journal of Marketing Research, 2012

sections.voiceover: So the real answer? Avalanche, if you trust your discipline. Snowball, if you've quit a plan before. Either beats paying minimums. Follow for the numbers.
sections.visual_cue: Two word chips: "AVALANCHE — discipline" and "SNOWBALL — momentum". Then channel name centered on #0A1020. Follow button animation.
sections.pacing_notes: Land the answer, then stop. CTA once, at the end.
